note: Negative vectors for the D8.19 projection wire. Each entry is a complete tampered record, stored as final bytes rather than as an edit recipe, because a recipe that matches nothing is a fixture that passes while asserting nothing. A consumer MUST check that `wire` differs from the named `base` in projection-vectors.json before trusting a refusal, and MUST require a refusal for every vector. `refusal_codes` records what the reference verifier produced; whether a code is normative is an open question, so a consumer should report code disagreement separately from the refusal itself.

vectors.name: a-lying-semantic-world-id
vectors.why: The record asserts a world id its own artifact does not hash to.

vectors.name: a-lying-execution-view-id
vectors.why: The V2->V1 projection is derived, so a sender's view id is a claim and not a fact; this one is false.

vectors.name: reordered-relation-bindings
vectors.why: THE TAMPER THAT MOVES NO IDENTIFIER. Every id stays correct and every binding stays individually true; only the ORDER lies. Order is derived from the semantic artifact, so canonical bytes catch it -- but nothing that checked the bindings as a SET would.

vectors.name: a-changed-relation-id
vectors.why: A relation id is derived from its allocation, never transmitted as authority.

vectors.name: a-changed-revision-id
vectors.why: Likewise a revision id, which is derived from the canonical revision.

vectors.name: a-changed-legacy-edge
vectors.why: The legacy edge is the JOIN KEY between a binding and the derived V1 artifact -- the field that must not be zipped by index.

vectors.name: an-extra-field
vectors.why: `execution_artifact` is the field the ruling kept OFF the wire. A receiver that accepted one has stopped deriving it.

vectors.name: a-missing-field
vectors.why: All five fields are required; absence is not a default.

vectors.name: an-unknown-projection-version
vectors.why: An unknown version must refuse rather than be read hopefully.

vectors.name: a-duplicate-json-key
vectors.why: A permissive reader keeps the last of two keys and discards the honest one; the exact reader refuses the bytes.

vectors.name: insignificant-whitespace
vectors.why: No whitespace is insignificant when the bytes ARE the identity.

vectors.name: trailing-bytes
vectors.why: A record is the whole input, not a prefix of it.

vectors.name: noncanonical-key-order
vectors.why: Denotes exactly the honest record, and is still not the record.

vectors.name: an-unsafe-integer-rounded
vectors.why: What a lossy reader WOULD have produced from a 2^63-1 rotor lane. The record stays well-formed and canonical; it is simply a different world, and now says a world id that is false. This is the C.4.1 defect turned into a test.

vectors.name: a-non-integral-number
vectors.why: A rotor lane is an integer; a fraction is not a narrower integer.
